tracks.name: Focus & Connection
tracks.blurb: A dog who checks in with you, loves your hands, and understands your marker words.

drill.name: Name Game (response to name)
drill.purpose: The dog snaps its head to you when it hears its name. This is the first 'recall' a puppy learns.
steps: Pre-load 5–8 treats in your hand. Sitting/standing doesn't matter; this isn't obedience.
Wait until the dog is NOT looking at you, then say its name once.
The instant the head flicks toward you, feed.
Repeat & treat.
drill.next: No distractions > gradually add distractions, close and at distance.
drill.tip: Name = 'head check' (look at me and wait for the next instruction), not 'come here'. In agility the name is a redirect.
gear: Treat pouch or a jar by the kitchen
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 3

bonus.title: See shaping in action
bonus.text: The Week 7 video: a 12-week puppy learns to back onto an object. Notice exactly when the trainer clicks and how the criteria change.

drill.name: Teaching 'Yes' (marker word)
drill.purpose: 'Yes' means the exercise is over and a reward is coming right now.
steps: Say 'Yes', feed a treat. Repeat until the treats are gone.
drill.tip: 'Good' is different: it means keep going, you're doing it right (continue the exercise).
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 3

bonus.title: Play the Shaping Game
bonus.text: From Week 7: one person leaves the room, the others pick a behaviour. Click only, with no words or pointing. You'll feel how much timing matters.

drill.name: Charging the clicker
drill.purpose: Teach the dog that the click always means a treat is coming.
steps: Have a handful of really good treats cut small.
Click once, then feed. The treat follows the click, not at the same time. Click > treat, click > treat.
Don't point the clicker at the dog like a remote; hold it at your side or behind your back.
Repeat standing, sitting, moving, and in different places.
A few times a day, 6–10 treats each. Done when the dog visibly anticipates the treat at the click.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Prep a week of treats
bonus.text: Week 2 says to have treats ready before every session. Cut a variety into pea-sized pieces and bag them 5–8 per exercise.

drill.name: Hand targeting ('Touch')
drill.purpose: Nose-to-palm touch. A portable focus tool, a distraction from trouble, and the first step toward contact training.
steps: Put a handful of small treats in one hand. In the other, hold one treat between two fingers of an open palm.
Present the open palm so the dog sees/smells the treat.
When the nose touches the palm, say 'Yes' as the dog eats the treat.
Wean the finger treat; present an empty palm and add 'Touch'. When the dog bumps it, reward by presenting the treat on the palm where they touched.
drill.next: Treat between fingers > empty palm with 'Touch'.
drill.tip: A great way to distract or refocus your puppy.
gear: Plastic lid as a hand-held target
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Work on your balance
bonus.text: Stand on one foot for 30 seconds while you brush your teeth, then switch. Next, walk heel-to-toe down the hallway.

drill.name: Cookie fingers
drill.purpose: A signal that means 'come to this hand, there's food'. The basis for luring and for many handling moves.
steps: Treat in hand, held at the dog's nose height.
Shake your wrist up and down as you move; the dog follows your hand.
Practise on both sides.
drill.tip: Teaches your dog to pay attention to your body language and the value of your hand. It's the beginning step for many agility handling moves.
gear: Soft treats you can hold between fingers
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 11, Sundog Foundation wk 13, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

bonus.title: Write down your verbals
bonus.text: From Week 3: name = head check, 'Here' = come right to me, 'Good' = keep going, 'Yes' = done, reward coming. Add 'Ready' and 'Get It'. Post them on the fridge.

alternates.name: Push Away and Run
alternates.purpose: Dogs want what they can't have; make that you.
steps: Gently push the dog away on the chest or side.
Run away and call.
When the dog catches up, reward with food, a toy, or lots of play.
gear: Tug toy for when they catch you
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 4

alternates.name: 'Find' / 'Scatter' (treats on the ground)
alternates.purpose: Permission to scavenge for a moment. Gets attention, removes attention from something else, and resets the dog's position.
steps: 'Find'/'Search' = throw one treat. 'Scatter' = throw 4 or more.
Example: release off a contact with 'Okay' then 'Find' (throw forward); next throw a treat behind the board so you can reload the target plate and the dog can re-load into 2on2off.
alternates.tip: Match treat value to how high the distractions are.
gear: Rug or yoga mat to scatter on (easier on paws, slows the hunt)

alternates.name: Informal 'throwaway' cue
alternates.purpose: Protect the value of the name and the formal recall by having a casual word for when success isn't likely or you aren't prepared to reward.
steps: Pick a short fun sound, e.g. high-pitched 'pup pup pup' or a kissing noise.
Use it to engage lightly when the dog may not respond to its name.
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Puppy K wk 1

tracks.name: Self-Control & Calm
tracks.blurb: It's Your Choice games: good things come from waiting and choosing well.

drill.name: It's Your Choice (the 'Mugging' game)
drill.purpose: Self-control taught through body language only: the treats are available when the dog stops trying to take them.
steps: Hold several small treats on an open palm in front of the dog.
If the dog grabs, nuzzles, paws or chews: just close your hand into a fist. Don't pull away. Say NOTHING; no verbal correction.
Open again. When the dog doesn't go for the treats, mark 'Yes' and, with your other hand, take one treat off the palm and feed it.
Repeat, rewarding every right choice.
drill.next: Move the open hand around: up, down, to the side.
drill.tip: Timing matters: open and close your hand at the right moment by reading body language. Dogs have about 1 second to connect a consequence.
gear: Somewhere to sit on the floor
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 4, Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Foundation wk 7, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9, Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Bake pumpkin oat treats
bonus.text: Mix 1 cup oat flour, ½ cup plain pumpkin purée and 2 tbsp xylitol-free peanut butter. Roll, cut small, bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Cool; keep refrigerated.

drill.name: 'Ready' / 'Get It' & 'This and That'
drill.purpose: Permission words. 'Ready' means get ready, look ahead and focus; 'Get It' means go ahead and take it. Builds excitement, self-control, and stops self-rewarding.
steps: Hold your dog's collar with one hand and a treat about 2 ft from their face in the other.
Say 'Ready'. When they're focused, release with 'Get It'.
'This and That': after a few 'Leave It' reps with a food container, say 'Ready'... 'Get It' and let them have it.
Use the same words for toys.
drill.tip: Use the words consistently. They tell the dog to focus and give permission to go.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 4, Sundog Foundation wk 6, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

bonus.title: Crate value video
bonus.text: The Week 3 video on starting dogs to value their crate. Watch how fast the reward follows going in.

drill.name: Leave it
drill.purpose: Don't touch that: food on the floor, a sock, a toy. A safety skill (e.g. broken glass with food on the kitchen floor), and later used in agility when a toy on the ground is the reward.
steps: Lead your dog to a food container (or a toy) and let them sniff.
Say 'Leave It' to redirect them, then feed a yummy treat from you.
Repeat a few times.
Then play 'This and That': say 'Ready'... 'Get It' and let them have it, so they learn the difference between not allowed and allowed.
drill.next: Increase temptation: open the food container.
drill.tip: Real-life payoff: food dropped on a broken-glass kitchen floor. 'Leave It' buys time to put the dogs somewhere safe.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

bonus.title: Calm breathing break
bonus.text: Five slow breaths: in for 4, out for 6. Dogs read body language first, so a calm handler makes calm games easier.

drill.name: Crate games ('Your In, Your Out')
drill.purpose: Make the crate a happy, safe place to drive into and wait in. Useful for class, trials, travel, and visiting.
steps: Throw a couple of treats to the back of the crate.
As soon as they're eaten, release the dog by throwing a treat outside the crate (or reward coming out with a quick tug).
drill.next: Build speed in and out. Once the dog drives in fast, add the verbal cue.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

bonus.title: Fill and freeze Kongs
bonus.text: Puppy K Week 4 uses a Kong to settle on the mat. Stuff three with soaked kibble and freeze them for the week.

drill.name: Mat work ('Go to bed')
drill.purpose: Going to the mat means lie down and relax until released.
steps: Lure onto the bed/mat while saying 'Go on your bed'. 'Yes' and treat when on it; 'Good' while they stay.
Release BEFORE the pup leaves: show a treat, throw it 2–3 ft away, say 'OK'.
drill.next: Lure into a down on the mat (don't cue 'down'); the mat should come to mean 'lie down'. Feed in position, then hold collar, throw a treat, release quickly before they break.
drill.tip: Don't cue 'down' on the mat. Lure into the down so the mat itself comes to mean 'lie down and relax'.
gear: Bath mat, towel or dog bed
Kong or chew for longer stays
drill.source: Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Rehearse It's Your Choice timing
bonus.text: Without the dog: hold treats in an open palm and practise snapping it closed and open fast. You have about 1 second to make the consequence clear.

alternates.name: Sit & position stays
alternates.purpose: Respond to the first cue and hold the position until released.
steps: Ask 'Sit' once at your side; if needed, lure into position with no extra hand signals.
Don't say 'Stay'/'Wait': the position itself means hold it until released.
Reward often while the dog is in position, then slowly build duration.
Add distance using the It's Your Choice open hand (see its progressions).
alternates.next: Puppy: sit, open hand with treats nearest the pup, one small sideways step. Break = close hand and reset; hold = step back, feed, 'Yes, Good Puppy'.
gear: Small treats in an open hand
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 7, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

alternates.name: Play & Settle
alternates.purpose: Teach a puppy to switch from excited play to calm, and to play with you appropriately (bite control).
steps: Play on your knees (taller = safer from face-biting). Gently push the pup away, wiggle fingers, provoke play.
Before the pup gets too wound up: hand in the collar (and hold the leash so they can't grab it), say 'Settle'.
When they relax, release collar pressure, say 'Yes', feed, and keep praising quietly ('Good boy, nice').
Restart play, then settle again before it escalates. Short spurts.
alternates.next: Use it whenever the pup gets over-excited and nips.
alternates.tip: No food in your hand while playing; it turns play into wanting the food.
gear: Treats in a pocket, not in your hand
alternates.source: Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

tracks.name: Body Awareness
tracks.blurb: New surfaces, shaping and back-end awareness: confidence and coordination for indoor days.

drill.name: Luring onto objects & new surfaces
drill.purpose: Confidence on different textures and objects; the foundation for perch work and contacts.
steps: Lure the dog onto and across the new surface; give lots of cookies even for trying.
Lure onto other objects and slowly increase the time they stay on.
Use 'Good' to say keep going, then 'Yes' and reward when the exercise is over.
drill.next: Lure onto more objects; longer duration.
drill.tip: Builds confidence; it's the first step toward perch work and contacts.
gear: Contact board if you have one
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Work on your balance
bonus.text: Stand on a folded towel on one leg for 20 seconds each side. Feel what your dog feels on a wobbly surface.

drill.name: Shaping & capturing
drill.purpose: Build behaviours from scratch, with no physical control or corrections, by marking small steps toward a goal.
steps: Capturing: wait for the dog to do the whole behaviour (e.g. sit), mark and reward it, then add a cue once it happens often.
Shaping: mark and reward successive small steps toward the final behaviour.
Novel-object starter: put an object down, stare at it. No words, no luring. Click & feed for looking at it, moving toward it, nose-touching it, a foot on it.
Raise criteria gradually. At each new level reward every time for a handful of reps, then reward randomly, then raise criteria again.
Add the cue only once the final behaviour is reliable; then reward only cued reps.
drill.next: Free interaction with novel objects (look, approach, nose, foot).
drill.tip: Shaping needs good observation and timing; it's the more advanced method.
gear: Pizza box or shallow cardboard box
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 11, Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 6, Sundog Foundation wk 7

bonus.title: Shaping Game, round two
bonus.text: Week 7's game again, harder: shape a family member to stand with both feet in a laundry basket. Notice how a late click sends them the wrong way.

drill.name: Clicker challenge: box & two books
drill.purpose: A body-awareness puzzle: clicker train your dog to stand in a box with all 4 feet, or with front feet on 2 separate objects.
steps: Review a nose touch on an object first.
Put down a shallow box (or two small books). No words, no luring.
Click & feed for looking at it, stepping toward it, any foot in or on it.
Raise criteria a little at a time: one foot, two feet, then all four (or both front feet on the two books).
Change the challenge each session, and bring your items to class to show what you've been working on.
drill.tip: Builds a thinking dog that offers behaviours, works through a hard task, and gains mental stamina.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 11, Sundog Foundation wk 12

bonus.title: Set up a clicker challenge kit
bonus.text: From Weeks 11–12: find a shallow box and two small books, and keep them in a bag with a clicker so challenges are ready to go.

drill.name: Perch work & moving off pressure
drill.purpose: Teach the dog it has a back end it can move independently while the front feet stay put, and to move away from handler pressure.
steps: Start once your dog happily stands on novel objects for a few seconds.
Lure, or shape with the clicker, the two front feet onto the perch.
Step into your dog. The pressure moves their hind end away from you while the front feet stay on.
When the hind end moves, say 'Yes' (or click) and reward.
Start with one step; over time build to a full circle.
Practise both clockwise and anti-clockwise.
drill.tip: Builds rear-end awareness, muscle tone, and balance on both sides.
gear: Perch or a sturdy upside-down tub
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 4, Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Load a feeding spatula
bonus.text: Week 2's tip: a spatula with peanut butter, cheese spread or cream cheese lets you reward without bending over. Great for small dogs and perch work.

drill.name: Contact training: 2on2off
drill.purpose: Stop at the bottom of a contact (dogwalk, teeter, A-frame): back feet in the yellow zone, front feet on the ground, until released.
steps: Sit on the ground in front of (later beside) the plank.
Lure the dog onto the plank with a treat at its nose.
Slowly bring your hand to the ground close to the plank so the front paws step down.
Praise and place a treat between the front paws; keep feeding there, with a new treat ready before the mouth is empty.
While the dog eats, move your hand away from the nose and back.
If the dog leaves, stop talking and lure back into position.
After a few treats, when the dog looks at you, say the release word and drop/throw a treat away from the plank.
drill.tip: Introduce the release word from day one.
gear: Sturdy board or the bottom stair as the 'contact'
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 18

bonus.title: Plan your contact cue
bonus.text: From Week 18: choose one release word for 2on2off ('OK', 'Break' or 'Alright') and use it from day one.

alternates.name: Hand targeting ('Touch')
alternates.purpose: Nose-to-palm touch. A portable focus tool, a distraction from trouble, and the first step toward contact training.
steps: Put a handful of small treats in one hand. In the other, hold one treat between two fingers of an open palm.
Present the open palm so the dog sees/smells the treat.
When the nose touches the palm, say 'Yes' as the dog eats the treat.
Wean the finger treat; present an empty palm and add 'Touch'. When the dog bumps it, reward by presenting the treat on the palm where they touched.
alternates.next: Treat between fingers > empty palm with 'Touch'.
alternates.tip: A great way to distract or refocus your puppy.
gear: Plastic lid as a hand-held target
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

tracks.name: Life Skills & Recall
tracks.blurb: Being caught, being handled, settling, letting go, and coming when called (hallway edition).

drill.name: Collar grab
drill.purpose: Make being caught rewarding, so the dog doesn't dodge when you reach for it. It's also the start of the drive/focus games.
steps: Touch/hold the collar, then reward.
Say the dog's name, hold the collar with a bit of pressure, feed, release the collar.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 4, Sundog Foundation wk 6, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Rehearse the vet hold
bonus.text: Puppy K Week 2's collar & body hold: practise the arm positions on a stuffed animal until they're smooth.

drill.name: Play & Settle
drill.purpose: Teach a puppy to switch from excited play to calm, and to play with you appropriately (bite control).
steps: Play on your knees (taller = safer from face-biting). Gently push the pup away, wiggle fingers, provoke play.
Before the pup gets too wound up: hand in the collar (and hold the leash so they can't grab it), say 'Settle'.
When they relax, release collar pressure, say 'Yes', feed, and keep praising quietly ('Good boy, nice').
Restart play, then settle again before it escalates. Short spurts.
drill.next: Use it whenever the pup gets over-excited and nips.
drill.tip: No food in your hand while playing; it turns play into wanting the food.
gear: Treats in a pocket, not in your hand
drill.source: Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Make a second tug toy
bonus.text: 'Out' trades need two equally loved toys (Puppy K Week 2). Braid two old tea towels into a tug with a handle loop.

drill.name: Tug & 'Out' (toy exchange)
drill.purpose: Teach the dog to play with you, tug, and let go on cue.
steps: Play on your knees (discourages face-biting). Wiggle the toy on the ground; push the pup away a little to make it more exciting.
Tug a few times, then stop and present the second toy while saying 'Out'. Hide the first toy behind your back if needed.
Repeat for a minute or two; stop before the pup tires or loses interest.
If teeth hit hand/clothes: hand in collar to stop (a toneless 'Ouch' or a Play & Settle), then restart. Biting ends the game.
drill.next: Adult dogs: let the dog bring the toy, tug a bit first, then 'Out' and trade for high-value food or another toy.
gear: Two equal tug toys (rolled tea towel works)
Hallway to keep the game contained
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 8–9, Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Brisk hallway laps
bonus.text: Puppy K Week 1: loose-leash walking works best at a 'late for something' pace. Walk 3 minutes of hallway laps with crisp 180° turns.

drill.name: Loose leash walking
drill.purpose: Walk with a loose 'J' in the leash.
steps: Start somewhere quiet (a hallway is ideal).
Pup on one side; leash in the opposite hand so it hangs in a 'J' from the collar. Treats in the hand nearest the pup (or a pouch on that hip).
Walk briskly, like you're late.
The moment the pup passes your hip, turn 180°, encouraging with 'pup pup pup'.
When they follow, 'Yes' and treat.
At first you may get only a couple of steps before turning; gradually go further.
drill.next: Once successful, move to more distracting places (e.g. back yard).
drill.source: Sundog Puppy K wk 1, Sundog Puppy K wk 3, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Read the toy drive handout
bonus.text: Re-read the Week 5 handout (Susan Garrett's 'How to Create a Motivating Toy'), then pick the toy and the drawer you'll use.

drill.name: Restrained recall
drill.purpose: Build a fast, excited recall to a specific side.
steps: Helper holds the dog. Step out about 30 ft (food-motivated dogs: show food first).
Without turning your body, look over your right shoulder (show your cheek), say the name, then immediately 'Here'/'Come'.
As you call, drop your right hand by your side and show the toy, so the dog comes to your right side.
On arrival: tug party (or jackpot several treats, excited voice).
Practise both sides.
drill.next: Puppy version: hold pup, handler runs away. Run > call name > 'Here'/'Come'. Look over your shoulder to the side you want.
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Foundation wk 6, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

bonus.title: Rank your rewards
bonus.text: Week 5: 'Here' is an emergency command used only with great rewards. List your dog's top 5 and save the top two for recalls.

alternates.name: Collar & body hold
alternates.purpose: A secure restraint hold for vet exams and handling; also helps with puppy biting.
steps: One hand runs over the back and under the tummy; the other under the neck and up toward the ear.
Hold the pup securely against your body for just a moment, talking calmly ('Good puppy, well done').
If calm and relaxed: put down, 'Yes', reward. Don't wait for wiggling; if they wiggle, try again and release sooner after they go still.
Optional: a helper rewards while you hold.
Gradually lengthen the hold. Goal: a secure, relaxed 'limp noodle'.
gear: A calm moment (after a walk or meal)
alternates.source: Sundog Puppy K wk 2, Sundog Puppy K wk 3

alternates.name: Meet & greet a person
alternates.purpose: Stay calm when a new person approaches.
steps: Step 1: Walk the pup toward a seated person who ignores it. At any lunge/jump, collar grab and 'Settle'; when calm, release pressure, 'Good puppy', treat.
Step 2: Pup in sit/stand/down; a person (no dog) walks toward you. If the pup gets excited, hand in collar and 'Settle'; reward calm.
If the pup won't settle: step on the leash and let the pup self-correct, no words; praise and treat the moment they settle.
Visitor takes another step with each success, until they can stand and chat. Later the visitor may offer a treat if the pup stays calm.
gear: A visitor who'll ignore the pup at first

alternates.name: Formal recall: 'Here' / 'Come'
alternates.purpose: Emergency-level cue: come right to me, fast. Possibly lifesaving.
steps: Use ONLY with great rewards.
With multiple dogs: name first (gets that dog's head check), then 'Here'.
Train it with restrained recalls.
gear: Your best rewards, saved for this
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 5, Sundog Puppy K wk 4

alternates.name: Building toy drive (Week 5 handout)
alternates.purpose: Create a dog that loves a special toy, for rewarding at a distance (sends, weaves, gambles).
steps: Keep the toy in a drawer in your main living area. The dog only sees it during this routine (and later at class).
Before meals, act goofy and say silly things on your way to the drawer; slowly open it.
Pause, then whip the toy out like you found $50 and run with it into the next room.
Swing and drag it on the line like a fishing lure, having a great time, but don't let the dog get it at first.
After 1–2 minutes, rush it back to the drawer ('oh no, it's gone') and carry on as normal.
Repeat 2–3 times a day. After day 2, allow a few seconds' grab, playfully steal it back via the line, play alone a bit, put it away.
Gradually lengthen real tug games with you.
alternates.tip: From 'How to Create a Motivating Toy' by Susan Garrett, handed out in Foundation Week 5.
gear: Throwable toy that doesn't roll (tug rope, ball in a sock)
3 m light line tied to it
A drawer to keep it in
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 5 handout, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

tracks.name: Agility Foundations
tracks.blurb: Flatwork you can do in a living room: position, sends, crosses and turns.

drill.name: Circle work (shadow handling)
drill.purpose: Build value for the dog's position at your side (the 'reinforcement zone') at any speed.
steps: Walk a circle around an object with the dog on the OUTSIDE. Clockwise = dog on your left.
Loose leash in the right hand; treats in the hand nearest the dog (tie the leash around your waist if feeding is awkward).
Feed constantly for correct position. High rate of reinforcement.
After 5–6 treats, break off and play (little tug games are good stress breaks).
Work both directions. No verbal corrections.
drill.next: Walk, dog on the outside, lots of food.
drill.tip: Be consistent all day: don't let the dog practise crossing your path or flicking away even when walking to/from the car or kennel.
gear: Kitchen chair or laundry basket to circle
Spatula with peanut butter for small dogs
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 2, Sundog Foundation wk 3, Sundog Foundation wk 4, Sundog Foundation wk 5

bonus.title: Footwork without the dog
bonus.text: Walk the Week 13 lap-turn pattern around a chair: back up, dog-side leg and arm back, wait, then step forward. Do both sides until it feels like a dance.

drill.name: Target plate: value & sends
drill.purpose: Teach the dog to look and drive ahead, independently of the handler, so you're free to handle.
steps: Load the plate with food 2–3 ft away.
Collar grab, say 'Ready' (= look ahead).
When the dog flips its head to the plate, release with 'Get It' and race the dog to the plate.
Move the plate further away as drive and speed grow.
drill.next: Collar grab > Ready > head flips to plate > Get It.
gear: Paper plate or plastic lid as target plate
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 10, Sundog Foundation wk 11, Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Foundation wk 18, Sundog Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Circle work video
bonus.text: The Week 3 circle work clip. Watch the dog's position at the handler's side on the curve.

drill.name: Blind cross on the flat (with restrained recall)
drill.purpose: Handler changes sides in front of the dog; the dog switches sides behind the handler's back.
steps: A helper holds the dog while you move forward.
Treat or toy in each hand, hands pointing down and slightly out at hip height.
Look to the side you want the dog on ('power of the cheek') and call its name. That arm guides until the dog commits to it.
After commitment, turn your head to the opposite side where you want the dog next.
Reward the dog at the hand that's out.
gear: A helper to hold the dog
Treat or toy in each hand
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 6

bonus.title: Why flatwork matters
bonus.text: Weeks 4 and 6: your dog spends more time between obstacles than on them, so that's where handling happens. Re-read those notes before class.

drill.name: Lap turn (cookie fingers)
drill.purpose: Turn the dog 180° away from you. Dogs naturally turn toward the handler, so this builds body awareness, two-sidedness, lead changes and following handling.
steps: Treat at the dog's nose height. Back up shaking cookie fingers so the dog follows your hand.
As the dog reaches you, keep drawing it past your hip, then turn it away by rotating your wrist (left hand = clockwise, right hand = counter-clockwise).
Once it commits to the turn, you both move forward, parallel. Feed.
Start slow; add speed once smooth. Practise both sides.
drill.next: On the flat: back up, turn 180°, move forward and feed.
drill.tip: Diagram: Week 13 lap turn steps 1–3 (lap_turn_week13_diagram.gif). Video: Week 13 Lap Turn.
gear: Cone, upside-down recycling bin or kitchen chair as the 'wing'
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 10, Sundog Foundation wk 11, Sundog Foundation wk 12, Sundog Foundation wk 13, Sundog Foundation wk 13 video, Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Foundation wk 8–9

bonus.title: Quick-feet drill
bonus.text: Three steps forward, pivot, three steps back, 5 times each way. Agility handlers need nimble feet too.

drill.name: Wrap (180° around an obstacle from the front)
drill.purpose: The dog drives forward to an obstacle and wraps tightly back around it.
steps: Handler and dog face the same direction.
Send forward with your guiding (dog-side) arm and leg, hand kept low.
Wait for the dog to commit ('lock on'/'hook onto' the obstacle) before moving ahead. Be patient.
When smooth, throw a toy ahead so the dog powers out; tug.
Build send distance to 2–15 ft without going to the obstacle's plane.
gear: Recycling bin, laundry basket or chair as the obstacle
drill.source: Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Foundation wk 14 video

bonus.title: Make target plates
bonus.text: Week 6's target plate: cut three plastic lids or paper plates and add a strip of coloured tape so your dog can spot them on any floor.

alternates.name: Staying connected & rewarding from the non-guiding hand
alternates.purpose: Balance handler focus with obstacle commitment so you can stay ahead of your dog.
steps: Look at the dog's path; your eyes draw theirs forward.
Stay connected ('power of the cheek'). You don't have to physically see the dog.
No sunglasses when working the dog.
From Week 18: stop holding treats in the guiding (dog-side) hand. Reward from the opposite hand, a target plate/food bowl, or a toy.
alternates.tip: A purely handler-focused dog must be escorted to every obstacle, which leaves you behind and pushing from the back. Value for going ahead and committing lets you get to the next obstacle first.
gear: Target plate or bowl on the floor
alternates.source: Sundog Foundation wk 14, Sundog Foundation wk 18, Sundog Foundation wk 6

bonusPool.title: See shaping in action
bonusPool.text: The Week 7 video: a 12-week puppy learns to back onto an object. Notice exactly when the trainer clicks and how the criteria change.

bonusPool.title: Play the Shaping Game
bonusPool.text: From Week 7: one person leaves the room, the others pick a behaviour. Click only, with no words or pointing. You'll feel how much timing matters.

bonusPool.title: Prep a week of treats
bonusPool.text: Week 2 says to have treats ready before every session. Cut a variety into pea-sized pieces and bag them 5–8 per exercise.

bonusPool.title: Work on your balance
bonusPool.text: Stand on one foot for 30 seconds while you brush your teeth, then switch. Next, walk heel-to-toe down the hallway.

bonusPool.title: Write down your verbals
bonusPool.text: From Week 3: name = head check, 'Here' = come right to me, 'Good' = keep going, 'Yes' = done, reward coming. Add 'Ready' and 'Get It'. Post them on the fridge.

bonusPool.title: Bake pumpkin oat treats
bonusPool.text: Mix 1 cup oat flour, ½ cup plain pumpkin purée and 2 tbsp xylitol-free peanut butter. Roll, cut small, bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes. Cool; keep refrigerated.

bonusPool.title: Crate value video
bonusPool.text: The Week 3 video on starting dogs to value their crate. Watch how fast the reward follows going in.

bonusPool.title: Calm breathing break
bonusPool.text: Five slow breaths: in for 4, out for 6. Dogs read body language first, so a calm handler makes calm games easier.

bonusPool.title: Fill and freeze Kongs
bonusPool.text: Puppy K Week 4 uses a Kong to settle on the mat. Stuff three with soaked kibble and freeze them for the week.

bonusPool.title: Rehearse It's Your Choice timing
bonusPool.text: Without the dog: hold treats in an open palm and practise snapping it closed and open fast. You have about 1 second to make the consequence clear.

bonusPool.title: Work on your balance
bonusPool.text: Stand on a folded towel on one leg for 20 seconds each side. Feel what your dog feels on a wobbly surface.

bonusPool.title: Shaping Game, round two
bonusPool.text: Week 7's game again, harder: shape a family member to stand with both feet in a laundry basket. Notice how a late click sends them the wrong way.

bonusPool.title: Set up a clicker challenge kit
bonusPool.text: From Weeks 11–12: find a shallow box and two small books, and keep them in a bag with a clicker so challenges are ready to go.

bonusPool.title: Load a feeding spatula
bonusPool.text: Week 2's tip: a spatula with peanut butter, cheese spread or cream cheese lets you reward without bending over. Great for small dogs and perch work.

bonusPool.title: Plan your contact cue
bonusPool.text: From Week 18: choose one release word for 2on2off ('OK', 'Break' or 'Alright') and use it from day one.

bonusPool.title: Rehearse the vet hold
bonusPool.text: Puppy K Week 2's collar & body hold: practise the arm positions on a stuffed animal until they're smooth.

bonusPool.title: Make a second tug toy
bonusPool.text: 'Out' trades need two equally loved toys (Puppy K Week 2). Braid two old tea towels into a tug with a handle loop.

bonusPool.title: Brisk hallway laps
bonusPool.text: Puppy K Week 1: loose-leash walking works best at a 'late for something' pace. Walk 3 minutes of hallway laps with crisp 180° turns.

bonusPool.title: Read the toy drive handout
bonusPool.text: Re-read the Week 5 handout (Susan Garrett's 'How to Create a Motivating Toy'), then pick the toy and the drawer you'll use.

bonusPool.title: Rank your rewards
bonusPool.text: Week 5: 'Here' is an emergency command used only with great rewards. List your dog's top 5 and save the top two for recalls.

bonusPool.title: Footwork without the dog
bonusPool.text: Walk the Week 13 lap-turn pattern around a chair: back up, dog-side leg and arm back, wait, then step forward. Do both sides until it feels like a dance.

bonusPool.title: Circle work video
bonusPool.text: The Week 3 circle work clip. Watch the dog's position at the handler's side on the curve.

bonusPool.title: Why flatwork matters
bonusPool.text: Weeks 4 and 6: your dog spends more time between obstacles than on them, so that's where handling happens. Re-read those notes before class.

bonusPool.title: Quick-feet drill
bonusPool.text: Three steps forward, pivot, three steps back, 5 times each way. Agility handlers need nimble feet too.

bonusPool.title: Make target plates
bonusPool.text: Week 6's target plate: cut three plastic lids or paper plates and add a strip of coloured tape so your dog can spot them on any floor.
